components.name: OpenMausBot's turn watchdog sleep rule
components.copyright: Copyright 2026 Milind Soni and OpenMausBot contributors
components.how: server/turn-watchdog.ts's sleep guard (e39d9b0d7, da0309f6c) translated to TypeScript: a look that arrives more than three intervals late is read as the computer having slept, and each running worker's clock moves forward by the gap instead of being stopped. Hivra keeps one interval of the gap as the tick's own, so a stall is still caught up to one tick late (WP-102). The rule lives in classifier.ts beside SILENCE_MS, so the headless watcher and the half-minute look share it.

components.name: Row-Bot's memory policy
components.how: memory_policy.py translated to TypeScript, its test cases ported, for WP-99. The semantic and graph score terms are folded into lexical matching, because Hivra has no embeddings and no graph; the store is scored in one pass rather than through a SQLite candidate query; Row-Bot's memory statuses become Hivra's: a fact with a removal waiting is archived, one with an update waiting is superseded, and an unreviewed proposal needs review. Hivra adds a small penalty for a memory that has faded, and scores the memories of every Mono a turn reads in one decision. Licence text in src/features/memory/model/LICENSE.row-bot.

components.name: Row-Bot's correction rule
components.how: learning/corrections.py translated line for line to TypeScript for WP-103, with its correction, not-a-correction and ambiguous cases ported to ruleCurator.test.ts. The store, episode and signal parts are left out because Hivra judges one turn at a time; the `<row_bot_turn_context` cut, the first-400-characters retraction window, the defect and asking sentence rules and the conservative order are the original's. Hivra adds its own fact detector beside it (remember that, from now on, always, never). Licence text in src/features/memory/model/LICENSE.row-bot.

components.name: Row-Bot's injection scan
components.how: external_content.py's injection scan translated to TypeScript, with its cases ported (WP-111). The fence and the warning sentence are not used. A match refuses a proposed memory and is noted on recall. It never deletes one. Licence text in src/features/memory/model/LICENSE.row-bot.

components.name: tasklane's protected paths
components.copyright: tasklane's LICENSE has no separate copyright line and the repo has no NOTICE file
components.how: crates/tasklane-core/src/paths.rs (protected_hits) rewritten in Rust for WP-158. Directory patterns match anywhere, secret extensions match, and a glob matches nothing. Hivra adds .hivra/, the hub tauri config files and the rule files, and compares built-in names without case. Rewritten from the work package because the upstream file was not in this worktree. The keyword floor in floor.rs is not included.

components.name: MiniMax Code's subagent-split-check, independent-review and taste-to-checks
components.how: Copied from stacks/ronny/skills at 88f84be7075106d8ce283e5d3a8138cdb8f9a205. The three named skills, plus the short long-session-check and context-tax-audit. Each file adds disable-model-invocation, so Claude Code does not offer it to the model itself; Hivra's skill index lists each one and where it is, and a first mate reads it when the work fits (WP-117). context-tax-audit turns two em dashes into a comma and a full stop. The skill text is otherwise unchanged.

components.name: models.dev's model catalogue
components.how: The models.dev catalogue trimmed to each model's context window and tool flag, at commit b4b8ca36 (WP-104). The generator and the provider files are not copied. The app reads the file offline.

components.name: Pierre Diffs
components.how: Pinned npm package for the optional split diff view (WP-116).

components.name: Row-Bot's MCP tool effects
components.how: WP-101: mcp_client/safety.py translated to TypeScript, with test_mcp_safety.py's cases ported. The verb patterns are written out as word lists; Row-Bot's interaction class is folded into a change so nothing but a read passes; and the provider's tool id is split into its server and tool, so a name-only read is trusted only for a server the person installed through Hivra's plugin flow.

components.name: Row-Bot's approval reviewer
components.how: WP-101: the rules of approval_review.py, and its answer reading with test_approval_reviewer.py's cases ported. Hivra asks no model to judge an approval, so only the checks a fixed rule can make are code, as a veto the decision path calls; the judgement rules are kept as REVIEWER_RULES for a judged step. Row-Bot's four levels are kept for narrowing.

components.name: Row-Bot's install scanner
components.how: WP-101: skills_hub/scanner.py translated to Rust, with test_skills_hub.py's cases ported. The thing scanned is a Hivra plugin, so no skills is fine and an unloadable skill only warns; a setup step the person already approves does not block; and the file list comes from the staged folder.

components.name: Row-Bot's proposal guard
components.how: WP-101: evolution.py's injection_problems translated to TypeScript, with its E9 cases ported. It checks what an edit adds rather than a whole draft, names each kind with a plain reason, and uses Hivra's own secret check.

components.name: Atomic Agent's fan-out contract
components.how: The contract's kinds of provide, its description and search-path rules, the contract block and per-task lines, and the requires-cycle walk (contract.ts); the wave planner and its cycle fallback (contract-waves.ts); the presence check of a provide in a file (contract-checks.ts); and the bounded quote of the person's request with its follow-up rule (worker-prompt.ts), translated to TypeScript at commit 1b4e641525c5b1427b48ff6b8d9932dc26bd8256 (WP-171). Hivra reads the contract from each task of one delegate_tasks call, refuses a requirement nothing provides and a provide nobody could check before anything starts, holds a task whose provider failed or did not deliver instead of running it anyway, fails a check that could not run, runs a declared check as the task's WP-40 checks gate, reads the request from the first mate's chat (the person's own messages only), and quotes it behind a mark on every line.
